k: A doubt that only comes after you have finished is not acted on (Ibn Baz; al-Mughni gives the same rule for tawaf).

After sunset on the {1}th the days of stoning are over, and a dam is owed by all for a day's stoning left undone (for a pebble or two the schools differ: see "Not sure how many you have thrown"). Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

At night: most scholars allow it for those who could not stone by day: the Hanafis (until Fajr, except on the {1}th), the Shafi'is, and the Malikis, who count the night as make-up time with a dam for the delay (Mukhtasar Khalil). The Hanbali school does not count stoning at night: it is done the next day after midday, the missed day first (al-Shinqiti, Adwa' al-Bayan).

Avoid pebbles from inside the basin, because they have already been thrown. The Hanbalis say a used pebble does not count (al-Mughni). The Shafi'is count it (al-Mughni). The Hanafis and the Malikis count it but dislike it: Malik told Ibn al-Qasim, who had lost a pebble and thrown one of the Jamarat pebbles instead, "That is disliked, and I see nothing owed by you" (al-Mudawwanah). The Hanafis also dislike taking pebbles from beside the jamrah (al-Hidayah). A pebble from anywhere else counts for everyone.

Found out later that a pebble was certainly missed? The schools differ. According to al-Mughni, Imam Ahmad's apparent view is that nothing is owed for one or two pebbles. The evidence given is Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA): coming back from the Hajj with the Prophet ﷺ, some said "I threw seven" and others "six", and none faulted the other (al-Nasa'i {1}; al-Albani: chain sahih; Zubair Ali Zai: da'if). Ibn Baz also excused a doubt about a single pebble. The Malikis owe a dam even for one pebble; the Shafi'is a dam for three, and a mudd of food for each pebble below that; the Hanafis half a sa' of food for each pebble, up to the value of a dam (al-Mughni). While the days of stoning last it can still be made up, and the order of the jamarat matters, so tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

Go by the number you are sure of and throw the rest. Unsure whether it was five or six? Count five and throw two more (Ibn Baz). The Prophet ﷺ gave this rule for doubt in prayer: "let him cast aside the doubt and build on what he is sure of" (Muslim {1}), and al-Mughni applies the same rule to counting the rounds of tawaf.
Hanafis: a pebble that lands just beside the jamrah also counts; one that lands far from it does not (al-Hidayah). Aim into the basin and every school counts it.
In the crowd, do not bend down to search the floor. Step out of the flow first, or use a spare: carrying a few extra pebbles helps.

It does not have to hit the wall: the wall only marks the target. A pebble that lands in the basin counts even if it bounces out again (Ibn Baz; Ibn Uthaymin; al-Fawzan). One that falls short does not count (al-Mughni). One that hits something hard or someone's clothing and then drops into the basin counts (al-Mughni; the Malikis likewise, Mukhtasar Khalil).

Missed a whole day? Stone it the next day after midday, in order: the missed day's three first (only Aqabah if it was the {1}th), then that day's. Shafi'is and Hanbalis: nothing more is owed. Hanafis and Malikis: a dam for the delay (Hanafis: nothing for the {2}th if you stone before Fajr of the {3}th).

Not sure it went in? If it most likely went in, it counts (al-Mughni). If you cannot tell, throw another: al-Shafi'i said it does not count until you know it landed in place (al-Umm), and another pebble settles it.

Pick up small ones rather than breaking a big stone, which can send a chip into your face (al-Mughni). There is no need to wash them (the Prophet ﷺ is not reported to have done so; some scholars recommend it).

Small: about the size of a chickpea or a date stone, the "pebbles for flicking" (hasa al-khadhf). When Ibn Abbas (RA) picked them up for him, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Pebbles like these. And beware of going to extremes in religion" (al-Nasa'i {1}, sahih per al-Albani). Jabir (RA) saw him stone the Jamrah with pebbles like hasa al-khadhf (Muslim {2}).
Stoned before midday on the {1}th, {2}th or {3}th? The majority count it as not done: repeat it after midday (Hanafis allow it before midday on the {4}th).

The times: on the {1}th, Jamrat al-Aqabah from sunrise until sunset (for the weak who left Muzdalifah early, Shafi'is and Hanbalis allow it from after midnight, Hanafis and Malikis only from Fajr). On the {2}th, {3}th and {4}th, from midday until sunset. The Prophet ﷺ stoned on the {5}th in the forenoon and on the later days after the sun had passed its height (Muslim {6}).

They count as one. Take the extra off your count and throw the rest one at a time, with "Allahu akbar" for each. The Prophet ﷺ threw seven pebbles one after the other, saying takbir with each (Muslim {1}; Bukhari {2}). This is the view of Ahmad, Malik, al-Shafi'i and the Hanafis; Ata' held otherwise (al-Mughni).
Throw another pebble in its place. Only a pebble that lands inside the basin counts, so do not add the one that missed to your count.
Throw stones, not shoes, wood or other things. The Hanafis also accept clay or anything else of the earth; the other schools accept only stone.

Too big or too small? The Malikis, the Shafi'is and the preferred Hanafi view count a bigger stone, though it is disliked. The Hanbalis say a very small or a big stone does not count: theirs should be "bigger than a chickpea and smaller than a hazelnut". A middle size counts for everyone, and a big stone can hurt someone in the crowd (al-Mughni).

Use another one. A pebble that fell from your hand was not thrown, so your count stays where it was. Any small stone counts, whether you picked it up at Muzdalifah, in Mina or on the road (al-Mughni reports no disagreement on this). The only question is a pebble that has already been thrown (below).

After midday: small→middle→Aqabah, in this order. One pebble at a time, "Allahu akbar" with each, into the basin. Dua after the first two, not after Aqabah.

Jamrat al-Aqabah only — the big one nearest Makkah. From sunrise; the weak who left Muzdalifah early: Shafi'is / Hanbalis from after midnight, Hanafis / Malikis from Fajr — if unsure, wait for Fajr. Stop the talbiyah at the first pebble.
